reason: The weighty bills are all about whether yeshiva students serve. Toward: universal compulsory service, the Ben-Gurion framework for deferral and exemption, integrating yeshiva students, and equality in the burden of service (rows 2, 4-7, 9-10). Away: the Basic Law on Torah study and the bill on the status of Torah learners, which make full-time Torah study a recognized alternative to service (rows 1, 3, 8). The statement asks exactly this, names the price and has one idea. Rows 11 (religious lifestyle in the army) and 12 (travel abroad during deferral) are slightly off-topic but light (2 of about 188 weight).
